clue.text: Not bright to put hydrogen in — it's blown up!

indicators.note: the phrase 'to put hydrogen in' tells us to place the symbol inside the dull word

parts.note: dingy means dull and dim, not bright
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen

explanation.surface: A warning that filling something with hydrogen is foolish, because it exploded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blown up' suggests an explosion, but the definition means inflated: an inflatable boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rubber boat is inflated with air, so it is something that gets pumped full before use.

clue.text: Home to the disgraced party, so huge disaster

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a wreck, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A party for a shamed figure turns out to be an enormous flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' is the anagram signal. Someone out of favour is said to be 'in the doghouse'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in disgrace is idiomatically being in the kennel, so a dog's hut is where shamed people live figuratively.

clue.text: European with refusal, wearing tat

indicators.note: to tat is to make lace by knotting thread, so the letters of the word before are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone from Europe says no while dressed in cheap rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tat' looks like a noun meaning junk, but here it is the verb for knotting lace, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Norway, a Scandinavian country, is one kind of European.

clue.text: Tramp dances without pianos

indicators.note: without means the named letters are dropped from the dances

parts.note: a hop and a bop are both informal dances
p is the musical abbreviation for piano (soft), so two of them are PP

explanation.surface: A down-and-out goes dancing where no pianos are playing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the two dances HOP and BOP, then remove both P's to leave the vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a homeless wanderer, the same as a vagrant or drifter.

clue.text: Final ascent, fell off backwards, fifty died

annotationWithheld.why: Final ascent, fell off backwards, fifty died: L (fifty) and D (died) end the answer and OFF reversed gives FFO, but no reading of 'fell' gives SCA; possibly an OCR misread, no blog found
annotationWithheld.clue: Final ascent, fell off backwards, fifty died

clue.text: Reported practice of closure at the very top

indicators.note: reported means the phrase is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: sealing is the act of closing something up tight

explanation.surface: A rumour about how things get shut at the highest level.
explanation.walkthrough: A ceiling is the upper limit, the highest level something may reach.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper limit or cap is the highest point allowed, the maximum.

clue.text: At which show that's reasonable, crushed

parts.note: ground is the past tense of grind, so crushed

explanation.surface: A fair-minded person flattened at some exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'a place at which a show happens', a site for a funfair or agricultural show.
explanation.definitionFit: An open site where travelling funfairs and shows set up their rides and stalls.

clue.text: Surpass alfresco occasion?

parts.note: a do is a social occasion

explanation.surface: Asking whether an open-air party beats the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass is to beat or exceed someone else's effort.

clue.text: Idly sketch interpretation of El Dorado, no painter

indicators.note: an interpretation is a fresh rendering, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no means the painter's letters are taken away

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: An artist doodling a version of the fabled golden city with no painter involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove RA from ELDORADO to leave ELDODO, which 'interpretation of' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To doodle is to draw aimlessly while thinking of other things.

clue.text: To invert tiny black holes is a bloomer

indicators.note: inverting turns the word for the eye openings back to front

parts.note: pupils are the small black openings in the eyes

explanation.surface: Turning over small dark holes is a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black holes' suggests astronomy, but these are the openings in your eyes. 'Bloomer' is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a silly mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Biscuit on Red Shirt

explanation.surface: A cookie sitting on a scarlet top.
explanation.definitionFit: A British biscuit filled with currants, and a loose red blouse named after the Italian general whose followers wore red shirts.

clue.text: First notes, one not right, wrong

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone's opening notes, one not right and simply wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' is the anagram signal, acting on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a song, the first music heard.

clue.text: Frank wants duck, then swan

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: A man named Frank wants a duck and then a swan.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name but is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank means being candid and honest, hiding nothing.

clue.text: Season and turn Chinese food

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: Instructions to add flavour and flip a dish from a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Season' looks like a cooking instruction to add salt, but it is a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: A crispy pancake wrap filled with vegetables, served as a starter in Chinese restaurants.

clue.text: Fish not interested, we hear, in plaything

parts.note: a skate is a flat fish

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said out loud and replaced by one sounding alike

explanation.surface: A fish shows indifference to a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A board on wheels ridden for fun, a toy or sporting gear.

clue.text: Heist finds sucker absorbed in drink

indicators.note: absorbed in means the sucker goes inside the drink

parts.note: a tick is a bloodsucking parasite

explanation.surface: A robbery uncovers a fool soaking in his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' suggests a gullible victim; it is a bloodsucking parasite.
explanation.definitionFit: A hold-up is an armed robbery, a raid at gunpoint.

clue.text: Victim of shooting has complaint

explanation.surface: Someone who has been shot has a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A game bird shot on moors in season, and a grumble.

clue.text: Amazing flier keeps time

indicators.note: keeps means the bird holds the time letter inside it

parts.note: a starling is a bird, a flier

explanation.surface: A remarkable aviator stays punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a pilot, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling is surprising or astonishing.

clue.text: Wielder of scalpel catches tail of giant fish

indicators.note: catches means the surgeon holds the letter inside
tail of means the final letter of the word giant

explanation.surface: A doctor lands an enormous fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giant fish' reads as one phrase, but 'giant' gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sturgeon is a large fish, the source of caviar.

clue.text: Steal a few bars

explanation.surface: Taking a short musical passage without permission.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab something quickly, and a short fragment of a tune.

clue.text: Bend a musical leg

explanation.surface: A dancer in a show strikes a pose on one leg.
explanation.walkthrough: HAIR is a 1960s rock musical; pins is informal British for legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairpin is a very sharp turn in a road.

clue.text: Close match about to demonstrate creative skill

indicators.note: about means the word for match goes round the other

explanation.surface: A tight contest is about to show some artistic talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close match' reads as a tight game, but the two words split, with 'about' wrapping one round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting and sculpture are the arts of beauty, made with creative talent.

clue.text: Work out to achieve shape

explanation.surface: Exercise in order to get in good condition.
explanation.definitionFit: To calculate or reckon, and a body's outline or form.

clue.text: Models, dancing ladies

indicators.note: dancing means the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Fashion models and women dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' suggests catwalk figures but means perfect standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are perfect examples or standards to copy.

clue.text: Beyond which castle entered stalemate at game

parts.note: a stalemate in chess is a draw

explanation.surface: A chess game where the castle moved as the match ended in deadlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle' and 'stalemate' suggest chess, but the castle is a real building, entered once you cross over.
explanation.definitionFit: A hinged bridge over a moat leads into a fortress when lowered.

clue.text: Smell of marjoram or all spice turning up

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top
of indicates the letters are taken from within the phrase

explanation.surface: The scent of herbs or allspice rising.
explanation.walkthrough: AMORA is concealed in 'marjoram or all', and 'turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant scent or fragrance.

clue.text: Mix in can

explanation.surface: Blend something in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend with a spoon, and slang for prison.

clue.text: Barrel for a fish

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel

explanation.surface: A cask for keeping a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish.

clue.text: Exotic greeting with a look that has no bounds

indicators.note: no bounds means the first and last letters of 'that' are removed

explanation.surface: A friendly welcome from abroad comes with a boundless look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' loses T and T to leave HA.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloha is the Hawaiian word for hello and goodbye.

clue.text: Something prickly cut back on posh tree

indicators.note: back means the word for cut is reversed

explanation.surface: Something thorny trimmed on a fancy tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses CROP to make PORC.
explanation.definitionFit: A porcupine is a rodent covered in spines.

clue.text: Plane's job to maintain Tory leader's status

indicators.note: to maintain means the smoothing word holds the letter inside

parts.note: a plane smooths wood, the same job as sanding

indicators.note: leader's means the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: A carpenter's work keeps up a politician's position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' suggests aircraft, but it is a carpenter's smoothing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing is reputation or rank in society.

clue.text: "Vessel almost vanished" in the vernacular

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A ship nearly lost, described in local speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon is specialised talk, language of a trade.
